note: What this file is: the second critique of the rebuilt notice corner (log 31 and 32): two critics and a skeptic, as they wrote it. Folder paths from the working session are shortened to SCRATCH.

result.verdict: NOW fixes the first rebuild's worst fault. Nothing clips any more: the notice paper went from 0.96–0.99 brightness with 20% of pixels clipped to 0.80–0.87 with none, the drum rim from 0.985 to 0.77, and the board behind the notice from 0.74 to 0.18–0.23. The composition still holds: the centre of the brightest parts (0.78 across, 0.57 down) sits on the notice's centre (0.79, 0.57), and the notice holds 57% of the brightest 3% of the frame. The light is not yet the reference's. The notice is flat peach from top to bottom (paper brightness 0.855 to 0.869, red-minus-blue +0.20 to +0.21), where the reference runs from 0.62 and +0.10 at the top to 0.75 and +0.31 at the bottom. Two causes: the fire's point light sits 72% of the way up the notice, and the 'from below' spot is aimed at a 0.36 m circle behind the chair back, so it whitens the chair and leaks through the board as an orange patch on the house wall. Three bright things still look wrong: the corner lamp's glass is a flat beige card (0.715–0.719 brightness in every row, the notice's own hue), the drum's inside is salmon pink and as bright as the notice, and the chair back is brighter than the notice it covers, so the two merge into one pale shape. The left side has less light than the reference's (22% of the above-average light against 39%), mostly because the reference's left gas lamp and the fire's warm patch on the road are missing; and the whole ground is warm brown instead of a cool night. Fix the two fire lights, the lamp glass, the soot inside the drum and the chair's tint before the paid repaint; everything else is cheap polish.

faults.fix: (1) FIRE_WATTS 160 → about 70. brazier_light is at z 2.93, 72% of the way up the notice (z 2.37 to 3.14) and 1.05 m from it, so it lights the top about 1.4 times as strongly as the bottom. (2) fire_glow_on_notice: spot_size from radians(20) to radians(50); aim it at notice_centre() - (0,0,0.25*BOARD_SCALE) instead of 0.36*BOARD_SCALE; NOTICE_GLOW_WATTS 480 → about 300; and light-link it so the notice is its only receiver. If light linking isn't taken, set use_shadow=True instead. Today its 20° cone makes a 0.36 m circle centred 7 cm above the notice's bottom edge, which the chair back covers. (3) Leave corner_lamp_light and dusk_skylight alone: neither can reach the notice's face. Aim for a top band of 0.60–0.68 with red-minus-blue at most +0.15, a visible lower third of 0.75–0.80 with at least +0.28, and nothing on the paper above 0.85.

result.not_checked:
I ran no Blender, so every 'aim for' value is an estimate from the light distances and wattages; none is a test render. I didn't see the plate: final/plate.log (14:09) has no finished picture, and notice-corner-plate.png (11:44) predates the fixes, so all plate positions above are my own projections from the camera start (2.99, 16.35) with the 64.4° lens.

Not checked:
- How the film engine lights the separately exported notice (signs.glb), and what its live fire light adds.
- The colour setting (view transform): I couldn't open street.blend. The flat 0.85–0.87 paper and the whitened hot core suggest a highlight-compressing transform like AgX.
- Whether light linking works in their Blender 5.2 EEVEE set-up; a cut-off distance or shadow-on fallback is given.
- How much of the warm ground is the stone's own colour rather than light.
- Rule 11 (first, middle and last frames of the slide), props poking into each other in 3D, the notice's text legibility, and the checker's code (I read only its report).

The reference's boxes were placed by hand, so its numbers carry about ±0.01 of position error; NOW's props were masked exactly with ids.png. Brightness is Rec.709 luma (0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B) on the picture's 0–1 values; 'warmth' is red minus blue on 0–1 values.

My measuring scripts and crops are in SCRATCH/plan3/corner/critique-31-light/work/.

result.verdict: NOW is close, and the slide itself is safe. The camera moves toward a point at 0.796 across, 0.500 down, which sits inside the board, so the board never uncovers anything. The near props only slip 8 to 48 px (of 1080) against what is behind them. The plate also covers the whole slide. Two things must still be dealt with before the paid repaint. First, the drum's mouth is a flat pale-pink disc as bright as the notice, because the coals sit too low to be seen from anywhere in the slide; a painter will turn it into a lid, and the live flames will stand on it. Second, nobody has yet looked at or checked the plate itself, and earlier plates rendered with these settings hit the "Shadow buffer full" fault. Five cheap 3D fixes would stop the painter inventing or merging shapes: a light leak on the wall in the phone-button strip, a chair as bright as the notice and fusing into it, a near-black lamp-post base under the board, shut gates lost in a black doorway, and the lantern's 1 to 2 px wire handle. Of the shot checker's six problems, none should change the scene before painting, and it missed most of the faults above.

faults.fault: The drum's mouth is a flat pale-pink disc with no coals or fire showing. It is as bright as the notice and reads as a lid.
faults.where: 0.457 to 0.674 across, 0.628 to 0.648 down. It covers 0.34% of the frame. Mean RGB is (248,191,165) and mean brightness 0.79, which is 1.01 times the notice's 0.78. The red channel reaches 255 there. 8% of the frame's brightest 3% lies on it.
faults.why_it_matters: The coal bed is 15.6 cm below the 0.856 m rim, and its heaped middle is about 10 cm below. The view over the near rim drops 0.176 m per metre from the end camera (6.9 cm below the rim at the drum's centre) and 0.126 m per metre from the plate camera (4.9 cm). So no coal shows at any point in the slide. What shows is the inside far wall, lit from 0.39 m above the rim by brazier_light. The painter keeps the plate's light and dark, so it will paint a pale lid or a bowl. The live flames will then stand on a lid, and the drum takes brightness away from the notice (rule 5). Rule 2's 'see into the drum' is not met, even though its oval check passes.
faults.fix: In assemble_notice_corner.py, raise COAL_TOP from 0.70 to 0.80 so the coal tops sit 5.6 cm below the rim, inside both sight lines. Lower FIRE_LIGHT_ABOVE_COALS from 0.55 to 0.45 so the light stays 1.25 m above the ground. Keep dark_every=1.33 so the bed reads as dark lumps glowing between, which avoids the earlier 'white stones' fault. Give the drum's inside faces a near-black soot colour. Target: drum mouth mean brightness at most 0.45, with only small orange hot spots and no channel at 255.

faults.fault: The plate, which is what the painter actually receives, has not been seen or checked. Its render setting is the one that failed before, and the exported files are stale.
faults.where: The whole plate: 1536 x 2730, taken 1.5 m back with a 64.4 degree lens. In it the story group spans about 0.52 to 0.84 across and 0.46 to 0.78 down. The notice is 0.126 of the frame wide, and the bottom 22% is bare ground.
faults.why_it_matters: The two earlier plate renders logged 'Shadow buffer full' 43 times (plate.log) and 32 times (plate2.log). That fault drew the hard black wedge. The checker only read the still's log (still4.log, no faults). The plate now renders with shadow_resolution_scale 0.70, which nobody has tested, so its shadows and light differ from NOW, the picture everyone judged. Separately, notice-corner-shot.json and the set and camera were exported at 11:44 and still give camera_end x 2.96, lamp_post x 3.5 and drum x 2.76.
faults.fix: When the running job (--plate ... --samples 64 --export --save) finishes, search its log for 'Shadow buffer full' and 'Could not allocate shadow atlas', and look at the plate. Run check-shot.sh with --view start and the plate as the finished picture, for the light rules (brightest parts, near white and black). Confirm that notice-corner-shot.json now reads camera_end 3.10, lamp_post 3.72 and drum 2.78. Do this before any paid call.

result.tool_check:
The checker's six problems:
(1) Left half holds 34% of the weight. This is real by its own measure but low priority. A painter usually flattens fine far brick and cobbles, so after painting the quiet side will weigh less, not more. Each small point light added there becomes a glow the painter can enlarge. If anything, raise left_houses_fill a little rather than add lights. It was also measured only on the end frame, not on the plate the painter receives.
(2) Notice only 0.07 warmer at the bottom. This is not real for the film. notice-corner.js gives the notice paper and the board their own surfaces, so in the film the warmth comes from its fireLight, not from Blender. Strengthening fire_glow_on_notice would also brighten the leak on the wall at 0.945 to 1.0 across. Judge this rule in the film's end frame.
(3) Pail should be 1.26 times taller, (4) notice 1.39 times taller, (6) lantern 0.12 m further right. These copy a sketch rather than fix faults. Stretching the notice would distort our printed sheet. Moving the lantern shrinks the 20 px gap from the board that the checker itself calls marginal. Leave all three.
(5) Lamp post 0.27 m to the left. The problem it points at is real, but moving the post sideways puts its black base behind the chair back, in the open gap under the board. Moving it back up the street to y 25.5 lands it at 0.81 across and hides the base for the whole slide.

What it missed:
- The drum mouth at the subject's brightness (it counts it as warm light inside the story box, so it passes).
- The light leak inside the phone-button strip: rule 12 only checks props' boxes, not bright patches.
- The chair brighter than the notice's median: rule 5's 'dirty the chair' is never tested.
- The black doorway with the gates lost, and the near-black lamp base inside the story group.
- 1 to 2 px parts (the lantern's handle) and stretched textures (the kerb).
- Render faults in the plate: it only read the still's log, while earlier plates logged 32 and 43 faults.
- The plate and the first frame themselves, which it never judged.
- Ghosting between overlapping near props.
- Stale export files.

My slide estimate, which also covers rule 11: the slide's vanishing point stays at (0.796, 0.500), inside the board. Measured against what is behind them, the drum's rim moves 12 to 20 px, the chair back 9 px (it uncovers notice, which stays sharp), the chair seat about 48 px, the pail about 37 px, the lantern about 21 px, and the lamp shaft 7 px sideways and 24 px below its head. All are in end-frame px. Where the lines meet stays at 0.684 across (0.670 in the plate's wider lens), because the camera does not turn.

result.summary:
Reviewer: skeptical senior. Folder: SCRATCH/plan3/corner/critique-31-review (work/ has my scripts m.py, proj.py, glb.py, glbtex.py and the crops; I edited nothing else).

New since both critics wrote: the plate finished at 14:25 (final/notice-corner-plate.png). Its log has 0 'Shadow buffer full' and 0 'Could not allocate shadow atlas' lines; the earlier plates had 43 and 32. Its light matches NOW: frame mean 0.238 against 0.248, paper 0.831 against 0.827, lamp glass 0.716 against 0.717. notice-corner-shot.json was rewritten at 14:25 (camera_end 3.10, lamp_post 3.72, drum 2.78). I measured the plate as well as NOW.

Verdict: NOW is not ready for the paid repaint, but every blocking fault is a few lines of the scene script. Six faults are confirmed in BOTH NOW and the plate and land on surfaces that wear the painting:
- the notice spot's light leaks through the board onto the house wall;
- the drum's mouth is a pale salmon bowl;
- the chair is as bright as the notice;
- the gas lamp's glass is a flat beige card;
- the lamp post's black foot shows under the board;
- the lantern's glass is milky white.
Two more need a test render: the gutter's step-like stripes, and the pure-black colliery doorway.

What the critics missed: the film never shows the plate's notice or board. In notice-corner.js the notice paper, the board timber and both posts keep their own surfaces (line 93). They are lit by a three.js fireLight placed at the Blender fire light's position (line 87: z 2.93, 73% of the way up the notice). So 'the notice is not lit from below' is real but is fixed in the film page, for free, after painting. It is not a reason to rework the Blender spot before the repaint.

Two root causes were wrong:
- The chair's glare comes from brazier_light, 0.60 m from the chair back against 1.07 m to the notice. It does not come from the spot: the chair back is 42 to 56 degrees off the spot's axis, and the cone's half-angle is 10 degrees.
- Raising COAL_TOP to 0.80 would stack the coal heap 2 to 6 cm ABOVE the rim, not 5.6 cm below it.

Numbers I could not reproduce exactly, though their direction holds (different definitions or thresholds):
- critic 1's left-half share of above-average light, 22% against 39% (I get 39% against 47%);
- cool pixels below mid-frame, 5.4% against 33.6% (I get 12.8% against 42.6%);
- the wall patch's area, 0.51% of the frame (0.99% with my looser threshold).

All other measurements match the critics to within about 0.02. My projection reproduces facts.json's on-screen light positions to 4 decimals.

NOT CHECKED:
- I ran no Blender (no blender process is running now, but the rule stands), so every target value is an estimate from light distances and wattages.
- Not verified: whether Blender 5.2's EEVEE honours use_custom_distance/cutoff_distance or light linking; whether one more shadow-casting light overflows the shadow pool; whether a 0.365 m liner clears the dented drum wall.
- Not checked for the lamp post at y 25.5: whether it meets a doorstep, downpipe or window, or catches the cottage_06 upper window light about 0.5 m above its new head.
- The cause of the gutter stripes (colour picture or normal map) is not confirmed.
- dusk_skylight's direction is not in facts.json, so I could not test critic 1's claim that it can't reach the notice.
- The lantern handle's pixel width: looked at, not measured.
- Critic 2's slide-parallax pixel figures: I re-derived only the slide's aim point (0.796, 0.500) and the lamp-foot projections.
- I did not render the film page.
- Not checked: rules 7 and 11 beyond the lamp column; props poking into each other in 3D; the notice's legibility; how the image program treats colour.
- Reference boxes were placed by hand (about 0.01 error).
fix_in_3d_before_repaint: 1. Stop the notice spot's light reaching the house wall (the most certain fault, and a one-line fix). Seen in NOW at 0.90-1.0 across, 0.54-0.80 down: a sharp orange oval, brightness 0.41, RGB 142,98,59, against 0.09 on the wall above it (0.94-1.0, 0.40-0.50). In the plate it sits right against the board's right post, at about 0.88-0.93 across, 0.57-0.63 down (0.36 against 0.08), and both paintings would turn it into a lit doorway beside the notice. Cause, checked by projection: fire_glow_on_notice has use_shadow=False (line 134), so its beam passes through the board; its axis meets the wall (x 4.15) at (4.15, 23.53, 2.23), which falls at 0.977, 0.649 in the end frame and 0.905, 0.608 in the plate. Change: after line 134 add `glow.data.use_custom_distance = True` and `glow.data.cutoff_distance = 1.4` (the notice is 1.02-1.2 m from the spot, the wall 2.1 m). If the preview still shows the oval, set line 134 to `glow.data.use_shadow = True` and add `glow.data.shadow_soft_size = 0.02`. The line-134 comment is wrong: the chair back is 42-56 degrees off the spot's axis (half-angle 10), so it can't shade the notice. Then search the render log for 'Shadow buffer full'. Target: that wall 0.12 or less.

2. Turn the drum's mouth into a dark, sooty opening. Seen in NOW at 0.458-0.675 across, 0.628-0.648 down: mean 0.785, RGB 247,190,163 (the notice paper is 0.827). The lip rows (0.626-0.632 down) read 0.85, with red at 255 on 73% of them; the plate's mouth is 0.764. Only 106 coal-coloured pixels show: the end camera looks over the near rim at z 2.455 at the drum's centre, and the central coal tops are at 2.45-2.48, so what you see is the far inner wall, 0.4-0.5 m under brazier_light. The live flames would stand on a pale bowl. Change: after line 123 add a black, faintly glowing liner:
`floor = bpy.data.objects['brazier_light'].location.z - FIRE_LIGHT_ABOVE_COALS - COAL_TOP`
`bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(vertices=48, radius=0.365, depth=0.13, end_fill_type='NOTHING', location=(DRUM.x, DRUM.y, floor + COAL_TOP + 0.065))`
`soot = bpy.context.active_object; soot.name = 'brazier_soot'`
`soot.data.materials.append(glow_material('brazier soot', (1.0, 0.3, 0.06), 0.15))`
The name must start with 'brazier' so notice-corner.js treats it as a near prop. Add fix 3's FIRE_WATTS cut too. Don't tint the whole drum: its outside is already 0.215, the reference's 0.21. Don't raise COAL_TOP to 0.80 (see rejected). Target: mouth mean 0.45 or less, lip 0.65 or less, no channel at 255. In the preview, check that the liner doesn't poke through the drum's dents.

3. Make the chair clearly darker than the notice (rules 5 and 9). The chair's brightest 5% reads 0.880, against the paper's median of 0.836. Where it crosses the notice (0.72-0.86 across, 0.605-0.65 down) it reads 0.815, against 0.829 for the paper beside it, in the same cream. It holds 24% of the brightest 3%, and the largest bright patch (0.648-0.881 across, 0.510-0.760 down) is 71% notice and 29% chair; the plate is the same. Cause: brazier_light is 0.60 m from the top of the chair back and 1.07 m from the notice's centre, so the chair gets about 2.6 times as much light per area. Because both are lit by the same light, cutting FIRE_WATTS alone dims them together; the chair's own colour must drop. Change: line 139, tint (0.52, 0.47, 0.38) -> (0.34, 0.34, 0.34). By my light estimate the critics' 0.42 still leaves the chair at about 0.64 of the paper's light, close to today's 0.79. Line 61: FIRE_WATTS 160 -> about 100, which takes both out of the highlight squeeze and also helps fix 2; try 70 only if the targets still fail. Target: the chair's brightest 5% 0.72 or less, and at least 0.12 below the paper beside it. Keep the notice at 1.8 or more times the frame average (now 3.13), and the checker's warm share at 1.5% or more (now 2.85%).

4. The gas lamp's glass is a flat beige card. It sits at 0.811-0.919 across, 0.148-0.224 down and reads 0.717 in every row (0.716-0.720, spread within a row about 0.02), hue 32 degrees against the paper's 28. It covers 0.57% of the frame and 8% of the brightest 3%; the plate is identical (0.716). The glass is opaque (its texture has no alpha channel), so all you see is the even glow. Change line 175: make_glow(m, (1.0, 0.6, 0.25), 0.6) -> make_glow(m, (1.0, 0.45, 0.12), 0.3). In the same branch add `m.node_tree.nodes['Principled BSDF'].inputs['Alpha'].default_value = 0.5` so the mantle (line 173, glow 8.0) shows through. Target: glass mean 0.45-0.60, a brighter core at the mantle, saturation 0.45 or more.

5. Hide the lamp post's black foot. In NOW it shows at 0.821-0.894 across, 0.677-0.736 down, brightness 0.049, 0.24% of the frame, between the chair back and the board's right post; in the plate, at 0.79-0.845 across, 0.625-0.669 down. It reads as an extra black pot. Change line 71: LAMP_POST = Vector((3.72, 23.25)) -> Vector((3.72, 25.5)). By projection the foot then sits above the board panel's bottom edge in every view (end frame 0.644 against 0.679, the film's first frame 0.620 against 0.637, plate 0.611 against 0.627), so the board hides it for the whole slide. The mantle moves from 0.864 to 0.811 across and 0.27 down: within rule 7's 0.07 of the notice's centre (0.797), and the glass leaves the 0.90 strip. y 26.0 gives more margin (film's first frame 0.611 against 0.637). Don't use the checker's 'move 0.27 m left' (x 3.45): the foot would land at 0.785, 0.66-0.73, right behind the lantern (0.72-0.80, 0.66-0.75). Afterwards check: the head is 0.71 times its present size; it stays clear of the winding wheels (their right edge is 0.714, the head about 0.77-0.85); nothing on the house front stands at y 25.5; and right_row_a_cottage_06_window_light_upper_0, at (3.7, 25.4, 6.36), is not lighting the lamp's cap.

6. The lantern's glass is a milky white bulb. At 0.728-0.787 across, 0.660-0.752 down it reads 0.846, RGB 235,212,193, saturation 0.18, maximum 0.998, with 6.9% clipped. Change line 155: make_glow(m, (1.0, 0.7, 0.4), 2.0) -> make_glow(m, (1.0, 0.5, 0.15), 0.8). Target: about 0.65, saturation 0.45 or more, and the flame (glow 30) the only near-white point.

7. (Test in the same preview; cause not confirmed.) The gutter channel and kerb nearest the camera show stacked dark stripes that look like steps or a grating. In NOW they are at 0.23-0.48 across, 0.93-1.0 down and at 0.38-0.46 across, 0.79-0.82 down. In the plate they are at 0.30-0.54 across, 0.70-1.0 down, in the bare foreground where the eye enters, which also falls inside the film's first frame (the middle 92% of the plate). They are on the street_channels ('channel_stones') and street_kerbs ('kerb_stone') objects from build_street.py. Change, at the end of build_scene(): in both materials set the NORMAL_MAP node's Strength from 1.0 to 0.3. If the stripes stay, they are in the colour picture: give street_channels the 'street_setts' material instead. If neither works, rely on the painter's words.

8. (Cheap.) Light the colliery yard so the shut gates read. The doorway at 0.57-0.64 across, 0.41-0.47 down reads 0.026, with 88% of it below 0.05, right beside where the lines meet (0.684, 0.439); the reference's doorway reads 0.109, with 1% below 0.05. The gates' bars and the coal tub only just show. Change: after line 210 add a point light 'colliery_yard_light' at (0.0, 77.0, 76 * RISE_PER_METRE + 3.0), between the gates (y 71.5) and the heapstead front (y 81.6): energy 40, colour (0.7, 0.8, 1.0), use_shadow False so it needs no shadow memory. Target: doorway 0.08-0.12, still below the frame average (0.25).

9. (Optional; keep only if it measures better.) This is the checker's rule-10 problem: the left half holds 34% of the weight. The road left of and behind the drum (0.33-0.50 across, 0.62-0.83 down) reads 0.21, below the frame average of 0.248; the reference's reads 0.44, 1.35 times its frame average. Try critic 1's spot 'fire_glow_on_road': at brazier_light's place, aimed at (1.4, 25.0, road height), which lands at 0.33, 0.66 on screen; cone 40 degrees, blend 0.8, about 250 W, colour (1.0, 0.45, 0.15). Keep it only if the checker's left half rises toward 40% and the warm share stays at 3% or less, and check the render log for shadow faults if you turn its shadow on.

ORDER: make changes 1-8, then a --preview of the end view, and measure the targets above with the same masks (ids.png). Then the 1080 still with check-shot.sh. Then the plate with RENDER_LOG=plate.log, then check-shot.sh on the plate using the plate's own camera: `-- --camera-at 2.9931,16.3538,3.1882 --yaw 6.87 --fov 64.4`, not --view start, which uses the film's 60.4 lens.
ask_the_painter: Keep every shape, edge and the light and dark exactly where they are in this picture; change only the painting style. Do not add, remove or move anything.
It is night. The road, the pavement and the house walls are cool blue-grey; the only warm light comes from the fire drum, the lantern on the chair and the gas lamps.
Do not paint flames, sparks or smoke, not in the drum and not from the chimneys. The drum's mouth stays a dark, sooty opening.
The gutter beside the kerb is a shallow, smooth stone channel: no steps, no grating, no drain.
The colliery gates are shut. Keep the doorway behind them dark, with the small coal tub just visible; no open tunnel and no lit door.
Keep the wall to the right of the notice board dark and plain: no lit window or doorway there.
Keep the sky plain and dim, darkest at the top left: no moon and no bright clouds.
The notice and its board will be replaced by our own after painting. Paint them plainly, with no new lettering.
Keep the lantern's thin wire handle exactly where it is, or leave it out; never move it.
leave: The notice is not lit from below (critic 1's first fault, the checker's problem 2). This is real in the plate: the paper's six bands from top to bottom read 0.813-0.840 with red-minus-blue +0.214 to +0.233, where the reference runs from 0.605/+0.09 to 0.729/+0.27. But the film never shows the plate's notice: the notice paper, the board timber and the posts are their own surfaces (notice-corner.js line 93), lit by fireLight at the Blender fire light's place (line 87, z 2.93, 73% of the way up the notice). So the film's notice will be lit from above as well. Fix it after painting, for free, in notice-corner.js: add a low warm light for the notice, for example new THREE.PointLight(0xff8a40, 2.5, 1.6, 2) at fromBlender([2.95, 22.2, 2.50]), and judge rule 6 in the film's end frame.

The board timber is orange-brown (0.22-0.24, red-minus-blue +0.19 to +0.23, against the reference's +0.08 beside the notice and -0.05 above it), and the left post is a bright 0.44. Both are their own surfaces in the film; they take the notice paper's tint (sameTintAs). If you want them cooler, change it in the page, not in Blender.
The notice is smaller than the reference's (2.1% of the frame against about 3.4%; height to width 1.40 against 2.06): a new notice layout is a content change for later. Don't stretch it.
Checker problem 6 (lantern 0.12 m further right): only 0.05 of the frame wide, and the board-lantern gap is already 20 px against the 18 px limit.
Lantern wire handle (1-2 px): it can't be deleted like the pail's because it has no object of its own. The painter's words cover it.
Ghosts between overlapping near props (chair/drum, pail/chair, lantern/chair back): rule 3 wants these overlaps. Look for ghosts in the weights-move view after painting.
The barrel is hidden behind the board in every view: harmless.
The wall under the lamp head is near black (critic 2): look again after the lamp post moves.

gas_lamp_1_light 260 -> 80 W for a cool ground (critic 1): leave it. The cobbles' own texture is warm (linear red/blue 2.04 after tint), so turning lights down mostly darkens the quiet side, against rule 10. Use the painter's words; or, in the same preview, try a cooler street_setts tint, (0.62, 0.62, 0.64) -> (0.55, 0.58, 0.66).

A relocated left gas lamp (critic 1's (a), gas_lamp_2 to (-3.03, 39.0), which lands at 0.25, 0.39 in the end frame and 0.30, 0.40 in the plate): only if fix 9 isn't enough. It would need the dustbins moved off its foot.
Red-channel clipping on the notice's hot core (0.768-0.851 across, 0.610-0.643 down, 793 px): it is on the notice's own surface, so it doesn't reach the film.
rejected: Critic 1: the 'from below' spot 'whitens the chair', and light-linking it to the notice 'removes most of the glare'. Wrong cause. I placed the chair back by projection: its top-left corner, at (3.31, 22.08, 2.66), lands at 0.761, 0.608, matching the picture. It lies 42-56 degrees off the spot's axis, and the cone's half-angle is 10 degrees. brazier_light, 0.60 m away, lights the chair.

Critic 1: 'nothing clips any more' and 'the paper 0.80-0.87 with none clipped'. The red channel is clipped on 0.12% of the frame: the notice's hot core (793 px at 0.768-0.851, 0.610-0.643, which is the spot's aim point at 0.796, 0.634), 73% of the drum lip's rows, and 157 px of the lantern.

Critic 1: the notice gradient, and the four-part spot rework (widen to 50 degrees, re-aim, 300 W, light-link), as 'must fix before painting'. The notice is its own surface in the film (see leave). Only stopping the wall leak is needed before painting.

Critic 2: the plate is unseen, has render faults and stale exports, and is a must-fix. This was resolved by 14:25: the plate exists, its log has 0 shadow faults, the shot json reads camera_end 3.10, lamp_post 3.72 and drum 2.78, and the plate's light matches NOW. Its suggested check, '--view start', would use the film's 60.4 lens; the plate needs --camera-at 2.9931,16.3538,3.1882 --yaw 6.87 --fov 64.4.
